title: fix(console): the settings hub tells a member that an administrator manages the settings
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zhuangjianguo"} -->
_Requested by **Steedos** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9Ubb?thread=cmsg_018ETKaNwMZCNRYD7D8Q9UbbDGjnwXxfMMqXVdUJCFtA1U)_

Fixes #29085

## What changes

- `ui/apps/console/src/pages/settings/SettingsHub.tsx`: an empty manifest list now has two messages. The hub asks `usePermissions().hasCapabilities(['setup.access'])`, the answer `MePermissionsProvider` already holds from `/auth/me/permissions`. No request is added and no server code changes.
  - A caller **without** `setup.access` sees an `Empty` panel, titled "Settings are managed by your administrator" with the line "Your account cannot view or change these settings. Ask an administrator if something needs to change." It uses the same `Empty` / `EmptyTitle` / `EmptyDescription` layout as the app-level "You don't have access" screen.
  - A caller **with** it, and no manifests, sees the reworded no-settings message: "No settings pages are available yet. They appear here when an installed app provides them." The old text, "No settings registered. Plugins can register settings manifests via the SettingsService.", is gone.
  - A caller who gets manifests sees the list unchanged. A backend that reports no `systemPermissions` fails open onto the no-settings message, as every `hasCapabilities` gate does.
- The capability is the exported constant `SETTINGS_DEFAULT_READ_CAPABILITY`. Its test parses it from `SettingsManifestSchema.shape.readPermission` in `@objectstack/spec/system`, so it cannot drift from the spec default.
- `ui/packages/i18n/src/locales/*.ts` (all ten packs): new `console.settingsHub.adminManaged` and `console.settingsHub.adminManagedDescription`; `console.settingsHub.empty` reworded.
- `.changeset/29085-settings-hub-admin-managed.md`: patch for `@object-ui/console` and `@object-ui/i18n`.

## Why

`GET /api/settings` (service-settings `listManifests`) lists only the manifests the caller may read. A manifest that declares no `readPermission` reads at the spec default `setup.access`, so a plain member is answered an empty list while settings exist. On the stock showcase that member read a developer sentence under `/_console/apps/com.example.showcase/system/settings`, as measured on #28988. The client can already tell the two cases apart from the capability set it loads, so the fix is on the hub alone.

## Verification

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

The Clause-② line follows the seat's claim amendment, made on this build's measurement: the built `dist/locales/en.d.ts` declares the two new keys as readonly literals, and the package entry re-exports `en` and `TranslationKeys`.

- New `SettingsHub.adminManaged-29085.test.tsx` (real `MePermissionsProvider`, five cases): member with zero manifests sees the member copy; admin with zero manifests sees the no-settings copy; admin with manifests sees the list; member with a readable manifest sees the list; the constant equals the spec default. **On `origin/main`'s `SettingsHub.tsx`, 3 of 5 cases fail** (the constant, the member copy, the admin panel); all 5 pass on this branch.
- `ui/apps/console/src/pages/settings/`: 33 files, 274 tests green. `packages/i18n/`: 95 files, 1443 passed, 13 skipped.
- Derived gates (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`, 34 families) at 86db0d24: all exit 0, the `pnpm --dir ui exec vitest run scripts/` suite included (169 files passed, 2 skipped). The PR-body gates (`check-changeset-no-major`, `check-adr-0087-registration`, `check-closing-keyword-parity`, `check-empty-changeset`) re-ran with this body on the merged head ad5601ca. `turbo run type-check` for `@object-ui/console` and `@object-ui/i18n`: 72 tasks green. eslint on the touched files: clean. `node scripts/check-sdui-manifest.mjs`: exit 0 (no registry change).

## Acceptance notes

- A manifest may declare its own `readPermission`. A member holding that capability gets that manifest listed, so the list is not empty and the member copy never shows. An admin who holds `setup.access` but lacks the capability every registered manifest declares gets the no-settings message, which is still true for them.
- Real-browser check on the stock showcase as member and admin: NOT MEASURED (it needs a full build and a running backend; the jsdom pins run the real permission provider).
